svg.title: What a node and an edge carry, and the two-hop traversal that pays for a graph store
svg.desc: Two parts. The first is the anatomy of the property graph model as implemented by Kuzu. A node is an entity — here a Company — and it carries properties: a name, a vertical, a funding stage, an outreach status. Person and Investor are the other two node types. An edge is a named, directed relationship — here backed_by — and in a property graph the edge carries properties of its own: the round, the announced date, and the source of the claim. Employs and invested_in are other edge types. The footnote records that this is specific to the property graph model; in an RDF triple store an edge is a bare triple and giving it attributes of its own requires reification. The second part is the traversal that justifies keeping a third store at all. Start at a company where an outreach reply already landed. Walk the backed_by edge to its investor — a hop a relational table handles comfortably. Walk the same edge type in reverse to a second company in that investor's portfolio that has never been approached; this is the hop that turns a long backlog into a ranked shortlist, because the untouched company is now a warm approach rather than a cold one. Walk an employs edge to the person to contact there, whose name and title come from public search. All of it is one statement in Cypher, where a relational store needs a join per hop written by hand. The footer records the correctness rule: every edge is parsed from a tracking record or a written research note and none is inferred by a model, because a fabricated shared investor sends a cold approach down a warm-introduction path that does not exist.
svg.text: THE PROPERTY GRAPH MODEL — KUZU, CYPHER
Both ends and the link between them carry attributes
THE SECOND HOP IS THE ENTIRE VALUE
